Bogotá: La Candelaria, Museums and Monserrate

After breakfast at the hotel, you’ll set out on a tour of the capital at the scheduled time.

Your first stop is La Candelaria, Bogotá’s best-known historic district. Colonial buildings, churches and narrow streets survive in this part of the old city.

A highlight of the tour is the Gold Museum. Its collection includes gold objects from the pre-Hispanic era and more than 20,000 pre-Columbian exhibits.

The route continues to Casa de la Moneda, a former mint dating to the 17th century. It occupies a colonial mansion near the Fernando Botero Museum. Botero donated a large collection of his work to the city, and the museum also displays pieces by Dalí and other European artists.

After the museums, you’ll walk through Plaza de Bolívar. The city’s main square is home to a monument to the first president and to Bogotá Cathedral. If the route takes you past the presidential palace around 5:00 p.m., you may see the changing of the guard.

The tour ends with a trip up Monserrate. The mountain rises about 500 metres above the city. At the summit stands the Cathedral of the Black Madonna, built in the 17th century. You’ll ride up on the funicular and take in panoramic views of Bogotá from the top.

The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays. Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum are closed on Tuesdays.

After lunch at a restaurant, you’ll return to your hotel.
